source: CASCADE (Guo et al. 2026) Case-Based Continual Adaptation for LLMs During Deployment
finding: CASCADE retains a new case only if the binary reward is 1. Failed attempts are never stored. Retrieval is a contextual bandit.
numbers: Macro success +20.9% over zero-shot on 16 tasks. Qwen3-32B, 12 single-turn tasks, 5 seeds: avg 66.68 CASCADE vs 48.33 zero-shot vs 63.76 NP-CBR (no learned retriever).
limits: Retain step is only 'reward==1 then append'. No dedup, no pruning, no cap. Only short horizons tested; authors list memory growth, case management, forgetting and learning from failure as open. Retention rule was never ablated against alternatives.
agent_relevance: Our S9 default (keep verified successes) matches the paper's rule, but the paper gives no evidence that this rule beats others. Treat as a baseline, not a validated policy.

source: CASCADE appendix C.5 human-involved revision (always retain the ground-truth case)
finding: When every case was retained with its true label (p_min=1), performance dropped on some tasks because the retriever could not manage the larger, more diverse bank.
numbers: Deterioration on MIMIC-MR, MIMIC-MSR, CMDL and LFD for both NP-CBR and CASCADE; Qwen3-32B, 5 seeds. CASCADE still beat NP-CBR in all settings.
limits: Retaining more (even correct) cases is not always better. Limited online timesteps; may be a retrieval problem, not a storage problem.
agent_relevance: Storing more verified cases can hurt if retrieval cannot sort them. Cap or index the case bank.

source: CASCADE ablation Table S5 (exploration and retriever variants)
finding: Having a case bank gives most of the gain; a smarter retriever gives a few points more. Retention itself was not ablated.
numbers: Average over 12 tasks: full 66.68; w/o Neural-LinLogUCB 63.76; w/o exploration 66.37; LinLogUCB 63.95; NeuralLogUCB 65.39; NeuralLinUCB 65.49; zero-shot 48.33. SPIDER 75.41 vs 66.87 without learned retriever.
limits: Qwen3-32B only in ablation; 5 seeds.
agent_relevance: Judge retention-policy tweaks against the large baseline effect of storing verified cases at all (about 15 points).

source: CASCADE coverage-gap theory (appendix D)
finding: Regret splits into a coverage gap (query space the bank does not cover) and retrieval regret. The coverage gap shrinks only if each query has some minimum probability p_min of becoming a retained case.
numbers: Sub-linear regret bound needs p_min > 0. With p_min = 1 (always retain a correct case) the gap closes fastest.
limits: Theory assumes retained cases are correct and the query distribution is stationary. Asymptotic, not small-budget.
agent_relevance: Retention must be tied to correctness. A wrong case stored breaks the guarantee.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following
finding: Agents copy the output of a retrieved case when its input is similar (experience-following). A bad stored case causes bad later outputs (error propagation).
numbers: Four agents: RegAgent, EHRAgent, AgentDriver, CIC-IoT. Input vs output similarity correlated across all evaluators. Error-free memory variant used as control.
limits: Partly synthetic agent (RegAgent); EHR and driving tasks are narrow.
agent_relevance: A stored case is effectively a vote on future answers. Admit only verified cases.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory addition results, Table 1
finding: Add-all is worse than a small fixed memory. Strict (oracle) selective addition is best. Coarse automatic filters are in between and depend on judge quality.
numbers: RegAgent SR: fixed 67.53, add-all 55.48, C1 63.18, C2 65.78, C3 67.35, strict 70.95. EHRAgent ACC: fixed 16.75, add-all 13.05, C1 26.19, C2 32.21, C3 34.66, strict 38.50. AgentDriver SR: fixed 40.11, add-all 32.32, C1 36.92, C2 40.01, C3 47.37, strict 51.00. CIC-IoT ACC: fixed 71.50, add-all 59.90, C1 74.00, C2 68.80, C3 79.50, strict 85.40. Memory sizes about 900-4100.
limits: Add-all lost 8-12 points vs a fixed bank in all 4 agents. A weak LLM judge (C1, C2) can be no better than fixed memory. Fine-tuning the judge on 300 trajectories (C3) nearly matched strict.
agent_relevance: The retention gate must be an outside check, not the model grading itself. A weak self-judge gives roughly no gain (G2, G5).

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory deletion results, Table 2
finding: Periodic deletion (drop never-retrieved) cuts memory about 65-70% with small loss. History-based deletion (drop records retrieved at least n times whose average utility is below a threshold) helps only with a strict evaluator.
numbers: Strict + no deletion RegAgent 70.95 (size 2938); +period 67.65 (949); +history 69.80 (2286). AgentDriver strict 51.00 (1178); history 51.81 (846). CIC-IoT strict 85.40 (904); history 89.60 (788); period 80.80 (310). Coarse C1 CIC-IoT: no deletion 74.00, history 73.70, combined 68.80.
limits: Parameters: n>=5 retrievals, utility threshold 0.5 (3 retrievals for AgentDriver); period 500 steps. With a noisy evaluator history-based deletion did not help. Future task outcomes are free labels, only if reliable.
agent_relevance: Log reuse count and downstream outcome per case. Prune cases retrieved several times that led to failure (the harm cases in SUBFIELDS).

source: Xiong et al. (2025) misaligned experience replay
finding: Some correct-looking executions are poor demonstrations. In AgentDriver, history-based deletion with a strict evaluator beat an error-free (ground-truth) memory baseline.
numbers: Appendix B.3. Figs 17-18 compare capped vs unlimited memory; read from text only, figures not inspected.
limits: Correct is not the same as useful as a case.
agent_relevance: Retention should score cases by observed reuse benefit, not only by 'was correct'.

source: Cao et al. (2025) ReMe: Remember Me, Refine Me
finding: Full addition (distil every trajectory) underperforms selective addition (distil successes only). Authors guess a single failed trajectory gives too little context for a good lesson. Similarity dedup is also applied.
numbers: Qwen3-8B BFCL-V3 Avg@4 / Pass@4: no memory 24.41 / 28.50; ReMe component variants 27.17 / 34.66, 28.91 / 36.67, 28.67 / 37.33, 29.00 / 40.67. Row-to-component mapping garbled in extracted text. Qwen3-8B + ReMe beats no memory by +8.83 Avg@4 and +7.29 Pass@4 on average.
limits: Success-only claim is stated as empirical but the exact rows could not be cleanly read. ReMe also uses failure-aware reflection, so it is not a pure success-only policy.
agent_relevance: Dedup by embedding similarity threshold is a cheap rule already tried. Failure lessons seem better distilled in batches than one at a time.

source: ReMe dynamic vs fixed pool
finding: A pool updated during use (add and delete) beat a pool built once, for all three model sizes on both benchmarks.
numbers: Qwen3-14B + ReMe(dynamic) Avg@4 44.66 vs Qwen3-32B no memory 40.89; Pass@4 63.71 vs 61.52. Qwen3-8B + ReMe Pass@4 55.03 vs Qwen3-14B plain 54.65.
limits: BFCL-V3 and AppWorld only; LangMem baseline was unstable across them.
agent_relevance: Online retention beats a frozen bank, when gated.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents
finding: Naively adding every successful trajectory already helps a lot. Retention curation adds more.
numbers: gpt-4o-mini. Naive accumulation: ALFWorld 73% to 89%, Wordcraft 55% to 64%, InterCode-SQL 75% to 79%. With database-level and exemplar-level curation: ALFWorld 93% (AutoManual 91% with a stronger LLM), SQL 0.82, Wordcraft about 0.69. Naive sits between fixed-DB pass@2 and pass@3; curated between pass@3 and pass@5.
limits: Diminishing returns with database size. Five-trial variance is large. 15-point ALFWorld gain equals a gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o upgrade.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that keeping only checker-verified successes works well; curation adds a few more points.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) exemplar-level and database-level curation
finding: Keep the trajectory per task with the highest measured usefulness as an in-context example. Best-per-task databases beat worst-per-task databases on ALFWorld and Wordcraft.
numbers: Fig 4: top-1 vs bottom-1 successful trajectory per task. Exemplar curation helped on SQL and Wordcraft. Database-level curation (population of 5, replace the bottom) raised the final score only on ALFWorld but helped small databases everywhere.
limits: Naive accumulation varied a lot across 5 trials because early cases shape later cases. Curation needs many training tasks and extra runs.
agent_relevance: Not every success is equal. Count how often a case is retrieved and whether the run then passed; keep the best per problem type.

source: Sarukkai et al. (2025) success prediction from the self-collected bank
finding: A classifier on task embeddings predicts agent success better as the bank grows, and is calibrated.
numbers: AUROC SQL 0.60 (100 tasks) to 0.77 (800 tasks); Wordcraft up to 0.71.
limits: Modest effect at small N.
agent_relevance: A bank of outcomes can feed a cheap 'will I fail here' signal for the impasse detector (G1).

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
finding: Rewriting past trajectories into abstract lessons degrades memory. Keeping raw episodes (cases) is as good or better.
numbers: Seven frameworks, five backbones. GPT-5.4 fails on 54% of ARC-AGI problems it had solved without memory, even when consolidating from ground-truth solutions. Utility rises, then falls below the no-memory baseline.
limits: ARC-AGI stream and a few other environments; GPT-5.4 as consolidator. Episodic-only control stays competitive with consolidators.
agent_relevance: Strong support for storing raw verified cases and not rewriting them. Our library should append, not summarize in place.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) ARC-AGI Stream with Retain, Delete, Consolidate actions
finding: When the agent chooses Retain/Delete/Consolidate it defaults to retaining raw episodes and does twice as well as forced consolidation. Disabling consolidation matches the auto regime.
numbers: Table 5 (GPT-5.4, batch 1, step 400): raw trajectories with no consolidation 76.6; append-only hiding prior store +26.8 over default; append-only with pruning +20.8; forbidding in-place rewriting +6.8. In-place rewriting is the most damaging single step. Abstract-only memory falls to the no-memory level.
limits: Even the best consolidation variant stayed below keeping raw trajectories. One environment family; separate effect of deletion not isolated in what I read.
agent_relevance: Direct experiment on retention form. Retain raw; delete rarely; gate any summarising.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Memento retains every case, successes and failures, with a reward label, and learns which to retrieve (soft Q). It is a rival to CASCADE's success-only retention.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%; DeepResearcher 66.6 F1 and 80.4 PM; case memory adds 4.7 to 9.6 absolute points out of distribution.
limits: Case bank saturates quickly: with about 3k training items no performance inflection was found as it grew. No store-all vs success-only ablation seen in what I read.
agent_relevance: Both rules work. The difference is where selection happens, at write or at read.

source: Memento retrieved-case count K sweep
finding: Gain from number of retrieved cases saturates at about K=4.
limits: Most of the gain (5.7 PM points) comes from the first retrieved case. QA tasks, modest bank.
agent_relevance: Beyond a few well-chosen cases per query, more gives little. Offer 1 to 4 cases.

source: Dual-memory framework for long-horizon LLM agents (2026) ALFWorld ablation
finding: Standard RAG over whole stored successful trajectories scored below the no-memory baseline. Stage-aware structure gave the gain, not volume.
numbers: 50-task ALFWorld subset: blueprint raises SR to 92; anchor-level retrieval 94; full system 94.78 vs w/o both memories 76.87; verifier rules 94 vs no rules 88 vs prompt rules 84.
limits: Only 50 tasks; no confidence intervals. Retrieval helps only when aligned with the current subgoal.
agent_relevance: Store case at the subgoal level with a stage tag, not whole-task transcripts. Fits our solved-subgoal library.

source: Yu et al. (2026) Self-Consolidation for Self-Evolving Agents (EvoSC)
finding: Removing either the success-experience or the failure-experience extraction hurts. Raw text replay runs out of memory as stored experience grows.
numbers: Llama 3.1-8B and Qwen 2.5-7B on DB, OS, KG. Gains +5.7% (Llama) and +10.6% (Qwen) over baselines. Baselines OOM at Exp=32 (DB/OS) and Exp=16 (KG) on Qwen 2.5-7B.
limits: Small 7-8B models with short context, so the OOM point is early. Authors' own method.
agent_relevance: Rival view: keep error-prone experience too. A compact failure note (trap) may be worth storing; test it.

source: Wang et al. (2026) ExpHarness / experience graph
finding: Stores skills from successes and lessons from failures in a graph, ranks by measured utility. Removing similarity filtering, graph diffusion or utility ranking lowers scores.
numbers: Four-variant ablation across QA, Reasoning, Coding, ALFWorld, AppWorld; per-variant numbers are in a figure, not read.
limits: Reward is with-minus-without-experience score difference. Authors' own system; figure-only numbers.
agent_relevance: Per-case utility measured by with/without comparison matches our reuse-count idea and was found to help.

source: Zhao et al. (2023) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Learning needs a pool of both successes and failures. An agent with only the initial few-shot examples gained nothing over ReAct. Retrieving by task similarity beat random and reasoning-similarity retrieval.
numbers: ALFWorld with Reflexion rounds: ExpeL retrieve-only 40.3, 47.8, 52.2, 54.4 over R0-R3; ExpeL+Reflexion 54.5, 57.5, 59.7, 60.4. Random success sampling dropped significantly (Table 3).
limits: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era; HotpotQA, ALFWorld, WebShop; few trials.
agent_relevance: Failures can be kept if paired with successes for contrast.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Retain only workflows from trajectories a checker judges correct. Online mode induces them from the agent's own judged-correct runs.
numbers: WebArena: 51.1% relative increase in success over BrowserGym baseline (12.0 absolute); 7.6% relative over hand-written workflows. Mind2Web cross-task step SR +24.6% relative. Rapid gain in first about 40 queries, then stable.
limits: Online induction depends on the evaluator being right. Low coverage on cross-task tests.
agent_relevance: A small number of early cases gives most of the benefit; a stable phase follows.

source: Smyth and Keane (1995) Remembering to forget: competence-preserving case deletion
finding: Classic CBR retention work on classes of case (pivotal, spanning, support, auxiliary) and a deletion rule that preserves competence. My fetch returned a different paper; not read. From memory.
numbers: Not verified.
limits: Do not cite numbers.
agent_relevance: Read next: tells which cases are safe to drop and which are critical.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-based reasoning: foundational issues
finding: Defines Retain as learning from the solved case: decide what to keep, in what form, and how to index it. Not opened this session.
numbers: None.
limits: From memory.
agent_relevance: Retention step should answer the same three questions: what, what form, indexed how.

source: Case-base maintenance literature (Racine and Yang; Leake and Wilson), pointer only
finding: Classical work on redundancy and maintenance of case bases. Not opened; subfield 07 covers it.
numbers: None.
limits: From memory.
agent_relevance: Link only; see subfield 07.
